verdicts.title: Convert ConversionInfo.num_bytes/to_bytes/from_bytes from broken classmethods to working instance methods
verdicts.issues: Verified end-to-end: before-snippet is verbatim (lines 53-81), all BEFORE AttributeErrors and AFTER outputs reproduce exactly on a patched copy (int num_bytes(5)->4, to_bytes(5)->b'\x00\x00\x00\x05', from_bytes->5), instance-level calls work for every registered pytype (int, float, bool, str; bytes/bytearray/memoryview are NOT registered -- set_conversion_info at pytypes.py:222 is commented out -- and ctypes types never go through ConversionConfig), grep confirms zero callers of these three helpers anywhere in package/tests/notebooks, and the full suite passes 854/854 on the patched copy (854/854 baseline on pristine). Class-level calls now raise TypeError (missing positional arg) instead of AttributeError, which is fine for instance methods with no callers. Notes, non-blocking: (1) for sub-byte types the repaired to_bytes emits MSB-left-padded bytes -- bool info.to_bytes(True) == b'\x80', not b'\x01'; from_bytes(b'\x80') round-trips to True only because bool(128) is truthy. to_bytes/from_bytes are value-round-trip-safe for all registered types but not representation-inverse for bool; worth a docstring sentence or a canonicalization decision at revision time. (2) Minor naming inconsistency: to_bytes's param was renamed to py_prim but num_bytes keeps 'typeinstance' (which also receives an instance, not a type). Style nits only.

verdicts.title: Fix bits_to_pytype docstring to document the real parameters (bits_obj: BitVector, pytype: type)
verdicts.issues: Verified: before-snippet verbatim (lines 303-314), sibling phantom-type line at 331-333 verbatim, and after application bits_to_pytype.__doc__ mentions bits_obj/BitVector and no longer mentions bytes_obj/py_prim_type/'thee'; 'PyTypeWithDefaultBytes' count drops 2 -> 0 file-wide. Docstring-only; suite 854/854. Two mechanical nits for the revision agent: (1) the 'after' field is not pure code -- it embeds a pseudo-diff comment block ('# --- and in the sibling ...') for the bytes_to_pytype edit, so a naive verbatim application would paste commentary into the module; the applier must split at that marker and apply the sibling phrase swap separately. (2) The sibling bytes_to_pytype edit is outside the finding's stated lines (302-314) but fixes the identical phantom-type lie and does not touch endianness semantics, so no overlap with the separate 'endianness' group.

verdicts.title: Make the registered str conversion a strict one-byte char: reject strings whose UTF-8 encoding is not exactly 8 bits
verdicts.issues: Fix verified: before-snippet verbatim (lines 207-213); every claimed BEFORE/AFTER behavior reproduced exactly on a patched copy, including to_bytes_aggregate(Rec('ABC',5)) now raising at serialize time, Rec('A',5) round-trip unchanged, to_bits_aggregate('ABC').to_bytes()==b'ABC' unchanged, and count_bits_in_unit_type(str)==8. Oracle claim checked: _legacy_aggregate.py IMPORTS these functions (lines 30-37), so oracle and public path move in lockstep, and plans.py compile_legacy_record_plan (lines 528-593) disqualifies any non-BitType field, so PyType records always take the reference path -- 'no oracle edit needed' holds. Full suite 854/854 (baseline also 854); plan_fastpath parity tests green and their randomized layouts genuinely use only INT/FLOAT BitTypes. Docs notebooks use only single-char strings. Substantive gaps the draft omits (flagged, not blocking under sole-user/loud-failure policy): (1) NEW bits/bytes divergence at the aggregate top level -- to_bits_aggregate has a 'str len>1 -> Iterable per-char' exclusion (_legacy_aggregate.py:255-257) that to_bytes_aggregate (line 359) lacks, so after the fix to_bytes_aggregate('ABC') (and iterables containing multi-char strings) changes from b'ABC' to ValueError while to_bits_aggregate('ABC') still yields b'ABC'; before the fix both agreed. The draft's rationale ('the engine's own semantics for str are char semantics') is only true of the bits engine. Revision should either mirror the per-char routing in to_bytes_aggregate (an oracle edit, triggering the sync procedure) or explicitly document/accept the divergence. (2) Residual silent-wrong on the bits path: to_bits_aggregate(Rec('ABC',5)) still silently emits 56 bits vs the declared 40 (per-char Iterable routing bypasses the new check) and only fails far-from-cause at from_bits_aggregate -- the finding's silent under-count is fixed for the bytes path only. PRE-EXISTING: str from_bits raises UnicodeDecodeError for any byte >= 0x80 (e.g. from_bits(BitVector(b'\x80'))), so the decode side already rejects half the one-byte alphabet -- this is the latin-1 question the draft's 'decision' field correctly surfaces for the maintainer.
